name: Shakta (Guru Archetype)
body:
Shakta are gurus that have dedicated themselves to meditation and working towards physical perfection in order to awaken and channel the cosmic energies of the divine mother that sleeps within themselves. This energy is called kundalini, but in some realms it is called serpent-power or serpent-fire. Shakta are constantly striving for enlightenment and use their bodies as vessels to reach it.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

The shakta guru gains additional proficiency with bagh nakh, chakram, gandasa, kukri, pata, tri-bladed katar, and urumi. Shakta gurus also gain Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat. They treat these weapons, their unarmed strike, and their natural attacks as philosophy weapons for the purposes of any abilities that rely on the use of a philosophy weapon (e.g. gentle fist).

Additionally, shakta gurus gain Autohypnosis as a class skill. This alters the guru’s proficiencies and class skills.

Kundalini Essence

Starting at 1st level, at the beginning of each of their turns while in combat, the shakta gains a single point of temporary essence, generally referred to as kundalini essence, which can only be invested in opened chakras. This temporary essence can be allocated as a free action as soon as it is gained, or as soon as a chakra is awakened, and lasts until combat ends, and then for 1 minute afterward. If they enter combat again before this minute has passed, the duration of the temporary essence is reset. If the shakta chooses not to invest this essence when they gain it, or if they have no open chakras, that point of essence is immediately lost. At 12th and 20th levels the amount of Kundalini essence the shakta generates each round of combat increases by +1.

If the shakta has multiple opened chakras or other receptacles that can accept this special essence, they can reallocate this essence normally between them as part of reallocating their essence. If the shakta suffers from essence burn, temporary essence gained from this ability is burned after any other temporary essence they possess, as well as after any other essence in their essence pool.

While not in combat, the shakta can meditate as a fullround action to draw out their kundalini essence , treating each round they meditate in this way as a round of combat. However, they can only generate a number of temporary essence in this way up to half of their maximum essence capacity,

Open Inner Chakras

Shaktas know a secret that even the most scholarly of viziers are unaware of. The chakra’s that support veilweaving are not the only kind that exist within a creature. At 1st level, as a move action that provokes attacks of opportunity the shakta can attempt to open their inner chakras, which reside within their soul.

Opening these chakras requires an opening check (1d20 + 1/2 their guru level (minimum 1) + their veilweaving modifier) made against its opening DC. For opening checks a roll of natural 20 is not an automatic success and a natural 1 is not an automatic failure. A shakta can attempt to open a chakra defensively, to avoid provoking an attack of opportunity. Doing so increases the opening DC by +5. Multiple chakras can be opened as a part of the same move action, with each opening check rolled separately, but they must declare they are doing so when making the attempt. The base DC of each chakra opened after the 1st increases by +1 for each chakra awakened before it as a part of the same action. Failing to awaken a chakra ends the attempt and the shakta is treated as having failed the opening checks to open each of the other chakras they were attempting to open after it.

Inner chakras must be opened in order of their rank, starting with rank 1 “root”. These chakras can only be invested with kundalini essence, but must be opened to be invested. As long as an opened inner chakra is invested it remains open, else it returns to a closed state and must be opened again to provide any benefit after a number of rounds equal half to the shakta’s veilweaving modifier (minimum 1 round).

If the shakta fails on their attempt to open a chakra they must attempt a Fortitude save against its opening DC or take an amount of essence burn equal to the rank of the chakra. If this would cause them to take essence burn greater than their available essence or temporary essence, or if they choose not to take the essence burn, they take 1d6 points of untyped damage for each point of remaining essence burn. If they fail an attempt to open multiple chakras at the same time they take damage based on the sum of the ranks of the failed chakra and the ranks of each of the chakras they were attempting to open after it.

Root Chakra Chakra (Rank 1; Opening DC 10): The root chakra is associated with instinct, security, survival, and potential for greater development. It energizes the desires of the flesh and distributes essence throughout the blood to circulate heat to the body. Kundalini energy is sometimes depicted as a serpent coiled around the root chakra, ready to ascend on a path from the body’s lower, basic urges and instincts to the heights of a disciplined and enlightened mind. By opening their root chakra, the shakta opens themself to an inflow of kundalini energy. The bloom of divine energy strengthens their aura, granting them DR/— equal to 1 + the number of points of essence invested in this chakra.
Sacral Chakra Chakra (Rank 2; Opening DC 13): The sacral chakra is closely associated with the generative power of the reproductive cycle, as well as pleasure, addiction, creativity, emotional needs, and relationships. When the sacral chakra is awakened, the adept recalls moments of sensual or creative ecstasy, when consciousness slips from the physical body into astral realms of weightless bliss. When opened, the sacral chakra gleams with sunlike radiance. By opening their sacral chakra, the shakta gains a fly speed equal to half their base movement speed, +5 ft. for each point of essence invested in this chakra with average maneuverability. Flight granted by this chakra must begin and end on a solid surface.
Navel Chakra Chakra (Rank 3; Opening DC 16): The navel chakra is sometimes called the power chakra, for it is associated with fire, combustion, digestion, anger, joy, fear, anxiety, and laughter. Here the serpent-fire swirls and swells with heat and vital energy, the source of the so-called “fire in the belly” of common parlance. Upon opening their navel chakra, the shakta can use a standard action to channel the divine mother’s energies as a breath attack that deals 1d8 points of damage in a 30-foot cone. This radiant gout of yellow flame somewhat resembles fire, but is untyped and bypasses all forms of energy resistance, protection, and immunity. The amount of damage increases by 1d8 for each point of essence invested in this chakra after the first.
Heart Chakra Chakra (Rank 4; Opening DC 19): The heart chakra is the seat of higher feelings and emotions, an inner realm of compassion, tenderness, love, and rejection. When infused with the substance of a creature’s aura, the energies of the heart chakra can take on powerful healing capabilities. Once the heart chakra has been awakened, the shakta can channel their kundalini into a torrent of healing energy as a standard action. They can use this ability on himself or touch any adjacent living creature with this energy to heal an amount of damage equal to 1d8 + 1d8 per point of essence invested in this chakra. In addition, they can remove one of the following conditions from the creature affected by this healing: confused, nauseated, sickened, staggered, or stunned. This ability has no effect on constructs, undead, or other creatures that are not alive. A creature can only benefit from this healing a number of times per day equal to the shakta’s veilweaving modifier.
Throat Chakra Chakra (Rank 5; Opening DC 22): Speech and hearing are nothing more than vibrations, and the throat chakra thrums with the occult vibrations that govern existence. Here the urges and emotions of the lower chakras give way to more refined, cerebral vistas, making the throat chakra the bridge between feeling and thinking. By awakening the throat chakra, the shakta can tap into the primordial mystical language underlying all things—the raw tongue of the multiverse that gives motion to atoms, keeps planets rotating in infinite space, and orders the coruscations of the stars. When using this chakra, the shakta slips into a kind of trance. They can take actions as normal, but they constantly mutter incoherent, often disturbing utterances of a vastly cosmic nature. Each round during their turn as a free action, they can select one enemy within 30 feet. That foe must succeed at a Will save to resist becoming staggered for 1 round. The DC of this save is 10 + the shakta’s veilweaving modifier + the number of points of essence invested in this chakra. This is a sonic mind-affecting effect.
Brow Chakra Chakra (Rank 6; Opening DC 25): Also called the intuitive chakra, this force center governs occult vision, both literal and metaphorical. Once the brow chakra has been opened, the shakta gains the benefits of true seeing out to a range of 120 ft., +5 ft. per point of essence invested in this chakra after the first. They also gain an insight bonus to Perception checks for each point of essene invested in this chakra. Engaging this chakra literally opens a shining indigo third eye of cosmic energy upon the shakta’s forehead. The mystical eye is easily perceived by anyone looking at the shakta, and persists so long as the brow chakra is open. Additionally, as a standard action the shakta can burn a point of kundalini essence invested in this chakra to cast one of the following spells as a spell-like ability while this chakra is open: analyze aura, arcane sight, aura sight, countless eyes (self only), share memory. Regardless of the normal duration of these effects they automatically end 1 round after the shakta’s brow chakra closes.
Crown Chakra Chakra (Rank 7; Opening DC 28): Channeling kundalini through all seven chakras at the same time aligns the shakta’s life energy to its utmost potential, bathing their aura in glimmering violet hues that illuminate their head like a gleaming halo. For the briefest of moments, they transcend mortality to become a being of temporary divinity. This alignment with the cosmic harmony of the multiverse grants them enormous sway over probability. Once the crown chakra is opened, the shakta becomes fully in tune with the powers of the multiverse. As an immediate action, a number of times per day equal to their veilweaving modifier the shakta guru can force a creature to reroll a d20 roll taking the shakta’s choice of the better or worse result. If the creature is unwilling they can attempt a Will saving throw to negate this effect (DC 10 + the shakta’s veilweaving modifier + the number of points of essence invested in this chakra). Additionally, once per day as a free action the shakta can burn a point of kundalini essence to gain an insight bonus equal to their veilweaver level +1 for each point kundalini essence invested in their chakras on any single attack roll, combat maneuver check, opposed ability or skill check, or saving throw roll. A roll modified in this way does not automatically fail on a natural 1. Using this ability immediately closes all of the shakta’s chakras. This ability replaces the guru’s philosophy.
Heightened Awareness

At 2nd level the shakta gains Psychic Sensitivity as a bonus feat. If they already possess this feat, or have access to occult unlocks via psychic spellcasting, they instead increase the number of times per day they can use each of their occult unlocks by 1. This ability replaces sunder veil

Fortified Body and Mind

At 4th, level traces of kundalini energy constantly suffuse the shakta’s being. They gain an insight bonus equal to their veilweaving modifier on saving throws against disease, mind-affecting effects, negative energy effects, and poison.
